meta.method: Individually written from official NHL scoring summaries and box scores, with NHL/team reports for historical milestones. Artifact identity follows the verified collection registry.
meta.writingReview: Reviewed against the supplied No AI Slop draft checklist.
meta.liveBoxscoreCheck: Existing 122 artifact stories preserved; 30 new artifacts checked against official NHL game summaries and box scores for 21 dates.

goal-1.title: Two goals, two very different moments
paragraphs: Marchand tied Calgary 2–2 at 1:36 of the second period, finishing a play credited to Brett Connolly and Zach Trotman. This puck is from that even-strength goal, his first of two that night. His late penalty-shot goal briefly put Boston ahead, but Calgary tied it with two seconds left and won 5–4 in overtime.

goal-2.title: A hand in the winner, then a goal of his own
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Patrice Bergeron’s go-ahead goal before adding Boston’s third at 9:04 of the final period. David Pastrnak supplied the assist on this puck. Marchand finished with a goal, an assist and five shots as the Bruins pulled away from the Islanders for a 5–1 road win.

goal-3.title: Three points on Bergeron’s hat-trick night
paragraphs: Marchand helped set up two of Patrice Bergeron’s three goals, then scored into the empty net with 1:01 left. His three-point night helped Boston beat the Islanders 5–2. David Krejci and Riley Nash earned the assists on this final goal, which ended New York’s attempt to close a two-goal deficit.

goal-4.title: Eight shots in an overtime loss
paragraphs: Marchand put Boston ahead 2–1 at 7:28 of the second period, then assisted on Riley Nash’s power-play goal for a two-goal lead. He finished with eight shots and two points. Columbus erased the deficit and eventually won 5–4 on Cam Atkinson’s overtime goal.

goal-5.title: Marchand touches all three comeback goals
paragraphs: Boston trailed Dallas 2–0 entering the third. Marchand scored at 1:17, assisted on Tim Schaller’s short-handed equalizer, then helped set up David Pastrnak’s winner with 12 seconds remaining. This puck began a three-point period that turned a shutout through 40 minutes into a 3–2 Bruins win.

goal-6.title: The Perfection Line makes it three
paragraphs: Bergeron and Pastrnak both earned assists when Marchand scored 58 seconds into the second period. That goal put Boston ahead 3–0 against Vegas, with all three members of the Perfection Line on the scoring play. The Bruins won 4–1; Marchand finished with three shots in 19:44 of ice time.

goal-7.title: The goal that got Boston to the shootout
paragraphs: Marchand’s power-play goal at 12:09 of the second period erased the Islanders’ 1–0 lead. Pastrnak and Torey Krug assisted, and neither team scored again through overtime. Boston won 2–1 in the shootout. Marchand supplied the Bruins’ only goal during actual game play.

goal-8.title: A power-play finish in Montreal
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 5:06 of the third period to complete Boston’s 4–0 win over Montreal. Pastrnak and Torey Krug assisted on the power play, giving Marchand career goal No. 237. David Krejci had scored 46 seconds into the period; Marchand’s goal made it two in the opening 5:06.

goal-9.title: A short-handed goal on a three-point night
paragraphs: Marchand scored short-handed at 12:28 of the second period, with assists from Bergeron and Brandon Carlo. He had already helped set up Boston’s first two goals, including Charlie McAvoy’s eventual winner. His goal made it 4–1 against San Jose, the final score.

goal-10.title: The only goal Boston needed
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 18:41 of the first period from a Patrice Bergeron assist. Neither team scored again. His goal stood for more than 41 minutes as Boston beat Arizona 1–0, with Marchand playing exactly 20 minutes and putting three shots on net.

goal-11.title: Two quick goals turn the game
paragraphs: Marchand tied Vegas 2–2 on the power play with 1:02 left in the first period, then scored again 33 seconds into the second. He also assisted on Pastrnak’s earlier goal. This puck is from the tying goal in a three-point night that helped Boston recover from 2–0 down to win 4–3.

goal-12.title: Five points at Madison Square Garden
paragraphs: Marchand scored twice and assisted on all three of Bergeron’s goals in Boston’s 7–4 win over the Rangers. This puck is from his first goal, at 1:08 of the second period. It put the Bruins ahead 2–1, just 57 seconds after Bergeron had tied the game.

goal-13.title: Marchand erases a two-goal deficit
paragraphs: Philadelphia led 2–0 after two periods. Danton Heinen scored first for Boston, then Marchand tied it at 12:22 of the third on an assist from Matt Grzelcyk. His goal forced the game beyond regulation, although the Flyers took the shootout for a 3–2 win.

goal-14.title: Career point 600 in Montreal
paragraphs: Marchand reached 600 career points with his goal at 19:23 of the first period in Montreal. It put Boston ahead 3–1, with Coyle assisting. Marchand also helped set up two Pastrnak goals, including one eight seconds into the second period, and finished with three points in an 8–1 win.

goal-15.title: An answer in Ottawa
paragraphs: Thomas Chabot broke a scoreless tie early in the third period. Marchand answered at 5:15, with assists from Anders Bjork and Sean Kuraly. Zdeno Chara scored 3:30 later, and Boston held on for a 2–1 win. Marchand’s goal brought the Bruins level before the winner.

goal-16.title: An early power-play lead
paragraphs: Marchand needed only 2:03 to score against New Jersey, finishing a power-play sequence with assists from Pastrnak and Matt Grzelcyk. Boston later led 2–0, but the Devils tied it in the third and won 3–2 in a shootout. This puck is the opening goal of the game.

goal-17.title: The empty-net finish against Pittsburgh
paragraphs: Marchand scored with 53 seconds remaining to complete a 4–1 Boston win. Pastrnak earned the assist on the empty-net goal. Pittsburgh had scored just 24 seconds into the game; Boston answered with four straight goals, with Marchand delivering the last.

goal-18.title: Marchand supplies the winner in Calgary
paragraphs: After six first-period goals left the teams tied 3–3, Marchand scored 52 seconds into the second. That was the game’s final goal. He also assisted on Bergeron’s second goal during Boston’s recovery from an early 3–1 deficit, finishing a 4–3 win with two points and five shots.

goal-19.title: From three down to an empty-net finish
paragraphs: Marchand helped start Boston’s comeback by assisting on Pastrnak’s second-period goal, then ended it with an empty-netter at 18:34 of the third. The Bruins scored five unanswered goals to beat Washington 5–3. This puck is the final goal, after Brandon Carlo had given Boston its first lead 71 seconds earlier.

goal-20.title: Twenty-seven seconds change the result
paragraphs: Marchand tied Philadelphia 1–1 at 12:01 of the third period, with assists from Pastrnak and McAvoy. Sean Kuraly put Boston ahead 27 seconds later. The Bruins won 2–1, and Marchand finished with five shots after scoring the equalizer with less than eight minutes left.

goal-21.title: A power-play goal keeps Boston close
paragraphs: Marchand cut Minnesota’s lead to 3–2 at 15:35 of the second period. Bergeron and Matt Grzelcyk assisted on the power-play goal. Marchand recorded six shots, but Boston could not find another goal in the third, leaving his tally as the game’s final scoring play.

goal-22.title: A point on every Boston goal
paragraphs: Marchand scored twice and assisted on Bergeron’s late goal in a 3–1 win at San Jose. This puck is his opener at 14:24 of the first period, from Jake DeBrusk and Erik Haula. After the Sharks tied it, Marchand supplied the third-period winner. He finished with eight shots.

goal-23.title: Marchand breaks the deadlock
paragraphs: The first period in Winnipeg ended scoreless. Marchand put Boston ahead at 4:42 of the second, with assists from Jake DeBrusk and Jack Studnicka. Winnipeg later tied the game 2–2 before two late Bruins goals secured a 4–2 win. Marchand recorded six shots in 20:41 of ice time.

goal-24.title: Two goals in a six-goal period
paragraphs: Marchand scored twice in the second period as Boston turned a 2–1 lead into an 8–1 win over New Jersey. This puck is his second goal, at 10:34, assisted by Mike Reilly and Bergeron. It made the score 6–1, with Boston still adding two more before the intermission.

goal-25.title: The first goal of a four-goal comeback
paragraphs: Pittsburgh had just opened a 5–2 lead when Marchand scored on the power play at 12:57 of the second period. Hampus Lindholm and Jake DeBrusk assisted. Boston scored twice in the third to force overtime, then Lindholm won it 6–5. Marchand’s goal stopped a run of four straight Penguins goals.

goal-26.title: Adding to the lead in Anaheim
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 6:20 of the third period, extending Boston’s lead to 5–1. Trent Frederic and Charlie Coyle earned the assists. His goal followed Pastrnak’s hat trick, and the Bruins added two more for a 7–1 win. Marchand scored on his only shot on goal.

goal-27.title: A tying goal in Tampa
paragraphs: Marchand brought Boston level at 1–1 with 3:02 left in the second period. Connor Clifton and Hampus Lindholm assisted on his goal. The Bruins tied it a second time through Pavel Zacha in the third, but Victor Hedman’s late goal gave Tampa Bay a 3–2 win.

goal-28.title: An early goal that held up as the winner
paragraphs: Marchand scored from a Bergeron assist at 2:54 of the first period in Nashville. Boston never surrendered the lead and won 5–0, making the opener the game-winning goal. Marchand played 17:38 and recorded three shots as five different Bruins scored.

goal-29.title: Scoring at even strength, creating short-handed
paragraphs: Marchand put Boston ahead 3–2 at 8:49 of the second period in Seattle, then assisted on Bergeron’s short-handed goal later in the period. The lead changed again before Boston won 6–5 on Jake DeBrusk’s late goal. Marchand finished with two points and six shots in an 11-goal game.

goal-30.title: The winning goal before Ullmark’s goal
paragraphs: Marchand scored with 35 seconds left in the first period to put Boston ahead 2–0 in Vancouver. DeBrusk and Bergeron assisted. Vancouver cut the margin to one in the third before goaltender Linus Ullmark scored into an empty net. Marchand’s tally stood as the winner in a 3–1 game.

goal-32.title: Two goals, including the winner in Los Angeles
paragraphs: Marchand scored twice and assisted on Pastrnak’s power-play opener in a 4–2 win over the Kings. This puck is his first goal, at 15:33 of the second period, which put Boston ahead 3–1 and became the winner. He added another with 2:12 left in regulation.

goal-33.title: Marchand closes out the Anaheim win
paragraphs: After Matthew Poitras scored twice to turn a 1–0 deficit into a Boston lead, Marchand hit the empty net at 17:26 of the third period. Coyle supplied the assist. The goal made it 3–1 and completed a three-goal final period for the Bruins.

goal-34.title: A power-play goal proves decisive
paragraphs: Marchand restored Boston’s two-goal lead at 9:51 of the third period in Dallas, with van Riemsdyk and Pastrnak assisting. The Stars scored with 28 seconds left, making Marchand’s power-play tally the winner in a 3–2 game. He recorded five shots in 19:26.

goal-35.title: Two points to earn overtime in Montreal
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Zacha’s goal 36 seconds into the game, then scored on the power play at 12:58 of the third to tie it 2–2. He had a point on both Boston goals. Montreal won 3–2 in overtime, despite Marchand’s five shots and 22:03 of ice time.

goal-36.title: Two shots, two goals in Colorado
paragraphs: Marchand scored on both of his shots in Boston’s 4–3 shootout loss. This puck is his first goal, a power-play opener at 11:21 of the first period with assists from Zacha and Pastrnak. He scored again in the third to force overtime.

goal-37.title: The equalizer brings career point 899
paragraphs: Marchand’s second goal of the night tied Colorado 3–3 at 5:46 of the third period. Coyle and Grzelcyk assisted. The goal brought him to 899 points, past Rick Middleton for fifth in Bruins history. Boston lost in the shootout after Marchand scored twice on two shots.

goal-38.title: Career point 900 comes on the opener
paragraphs: Marchand reached 900 NHL points by scoring at 5:02 of the first period in St. Louis, with Coyle assisting. He added a power-play goal in the third for another Boston lead. McAvoy eventually settled a 4–3 game in overtime; Marchand finished with two goals and five shots.

goal-39.title: Two goals erase Carolina’s lead
paragraphs: Boston entered the third period down 2–0. Marchand scored at 1:30, then again at 7:20 to tie it. This puck is the first of those goals, assisted by Frederic and Lindholm. Carolina recovered to win 3–2 on Jordan Martinook’s goal with 2:27 remaining.

goal-40.title: Marchand opens Boston’s three-goal period
paragraphs: Marchand scored 25 seconds into the second period in Edmonton to give Boston a 2–1 lead. Danton Heinen and Mason Lohrei assisted. The Bruins stretched the lead to 4–1, but needed McAvoy’s overtime goal to win 6–5 after Edmonton twice drew level in the third.

goal-41.title: Short-handed in Pittsburgh
paragraphs: Marchand scored short-handed at 14:54 of the second period, with Coyle assisting. The goal extended Boston’s lead to 4–1 during a four-goal period for the Bruins. Pittsburgh later pulled within one, but Boston won 6–4. Marchand finished with four shots and career goal No. 401.

goal-42.title: Goal 403 moves Marchand past Middleton
paragraphs: Marchand’s power-play goal moved him ahead of Rick Middleton into fourth on Boston’s career goals list. It tied Carolina 1–1 at 13:11 of the first period, with Pastrnak and Elias Lindholm assisting. The Hurricanes won 8–2. This is the goal-scored puck; artifact 316 separately marks the milestone with a game-used puck.

goal-43.title: One shot, the winning goal
paragraphs: Marchand broke a 1–1 tie in Detroit at 11:30 of the third period. Andrew Peeke and Pastrnak earned the assists. It was Marchand’s only shot on goal, and it decided a 2–1 Boston win after neither team had scored since the final minute of the first period.

goal-44.title: The first of two in 2:05
paragraphs: Marchand gave Boston a 2–1 lead at 2:58 of the second period in Chicago, then scored again just 2:05 later. This puck is the first goal, assisted by Pastrnak and Mason Lohrei. Marchand and Morgan Geekie each scored twice in the Bruins’ 4–2 win.

goal-45.title: Marchand’s second goal becomes the winner
paragraphs: At 5:03 of the second period, Marchand scored his second goal in 2:05 to put Boston ahead 3–1 in Chicago. Pastrnak and Jordan Oesterle assisted. Boston won 4–2, making this Marchand’s 81st Bruins game-winner, tied with Bergeron for second in team history.

goal-46.title: A record-tying penalty shot
paragraphs: Marchand converted his seventh career penalty shot, tying Pavel Bure’s NHL record. At 10:28 of the second period, he cut Seattle’s lead to 2–1. It was Boston’s only goal in a 5–1 defeat. This puck records the unassisted penalty-shot goal, rather than an ordinary even-strength scoring play.

goal-47.title: A two-point night against Tampa Bay
paragraphs: Marchand scored from a Pastrnak assist at 1:13 of the second period to put Boston ahead 3–0. His goal became the winner in a 6–2 game. He later assisted on Zacha’s short-handed empty-net goal, finishing with two points in 19:23 of ice time.

goal-48.title: A game-used puck from the Buffalo loss
paragraphs: Marchand scored Boston’s second goal on the power play at 10:13 of the third period, with Elias Lindholm and Pastrnak assisting. It cut Buffalo’s lead to 4–2, but the Sabres answered 30 seconds later and won 7–2. This artifact is a game-used puck from that night, not the puck from Marchand’s goal.

goal-49.title: Remembering the two-goal night in Chicago
paragraphs: Marchand scored twice early in the second period, changing a 1–1 tie into a 3–1 Boston lead. His second goal held up as the winner in a 4–2 game. This game-used puck commemorates that performance; the two goal-scored pucks are cataloged separately as artifacts 44 and 45.

goal-50.title: Two goals, one puck, on the road to the Cup
paragraphs: This rare Double Goal puck carries two scoring moments from Boston’s 2011 Stanley Cup run. Its Letter of Authenticity identifies Chris Kelly’s goal at 12:50 and Marchand’s equalizer at 14:15 of the first period — just 85 seconds apart. Bergeron and Mark Recchi assisted on Marchand’s fourth goal of the playoffs. Boston erased Philadelphia’s 2–0 lead and won 3–2 on David Krejci’s overtime goal.

sources.label: MeiGray Letter of Authenticity — Double Goal puck

goal-51.title: The Perfection Line delivers late
paragraphs: Marchand scored with 2:33 remaining to break a 1–1 tie in Ottawa. Bergeron and Pastrnak both earned assists on the winning play. Boston won 2–1, with Marchand scoring on his only shot of the game after the Bruins had entered the third period trailing by one.

goal-52.title: Three points with Boston facing elimination
paragraphs: Marchand scored twice and assisted on another goal as Boston beat Toronto 4–2 to force Game 7. This puck is his power-play equalizer at 11:23 of the first period, assisted by Bergeron. He later helped set up Krug’s go-ahead goal and scored into the empty net with 1:54 left.

goal-53.title: Marchand puts Boston ahead in a third-period comeback
paragraphs: Carolina led 2–0 after two periods. Marchand scored at 11:40 of the third to give Boston its first lead, following goals from DeBrusk and Connor Clifton. Krug supplied the assist. DeBrusk added another, and the Bruins held on for a 4–3 playoff win after scoring four times in 6:51.

goal-54.title: Two Marchand goals, then overtime
paragraphs: Marchand’s power-play goal at 14:33 of the second period put Boston ahead 2–1 against Tampa Bay. He scored again with 3:58 left in regulation to tie it 3–3. This puck is the first of his two goals. Ondrej Palat eventually gave Tampa Bay a 4–3 overtime win.

goal-55.title: The power play breaks a scoreless tie
paragraphs: Marchand opened the scoring at 8:00 of the second period against Washington, with Pastrnak and McAvoy assisting. Boston added two goals in the first 1:03 of the third and won 4–1. Marchand’s power-play goal ended more than 28 scoreless minutes to begin the playoff game.

goal-56.title: Marchand opens the scoring in Florida
paragraphs: Marchand put Boston ahead on the power play at 9:45 of the first period, with Zacha and Tyler Bertuzzi assisting. The Bruins never trailed and won 6–2, with DeBrusk and Taylor Hall each scoring twice. Marchand finished with three shots and 20:01 of ice time.

goal-57.title: An assist on Boston’s only goal in Utah
paragraphs: Marchand earned the lone assist on Cole Koepke’s goal at 12:49 of the second period. Boston held that 1–0 lead until Utah tied it with 5:09 left in regulation, then lost 2–1 in overtime. This puck represents Marchand’s assist on the opening goal, not a Marchand goal.

goal-58.title: A goal for Canada in the 4 Nations opener
paragraphs: Marchand put Canada ahead 2–0 at 13:15 of the first period against Sweden. Brayden Point and Seth Jarvis assisted on his goal. Sweden later erased a 3–1 deficit, but Mitch Marner scored at 6:06 of overtime for a 4–3 Canada win. Marchand recorded two shots in 11:22.

goal-59.title: Two assists on his return to Boston
paragraphs: Marchand helped Florida score 61 seconds into the game, then assisted on Eetu Luostarinen’s goal at 9:58 of the third to restore a 3–2 lead. This puck is from Luostarinen’s goal. Florida won 4–3 on Carter Verhaeghe’s goal with 26 seconds left; Marchand finished with two assists against his former team.

goal-60.title: Starting the comeback against Florida
paragraphs: Boston trailed 2–0 after the first period. Marchand scored at 3:38 of the second, assisted by DeBrusk and Coyle, to cut the deficit in half. McAvoy tied it in the third, and Zacha completed the comeback in overtime for a 3–2 Bruins win.

goal-62.title: Florida’s lone goal in Detroit
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 14:05 of the second period to cut Detroit’s lead to 2–1. Anton Lundell earned the assist. Florida stayed within one until the final two minutes, when Detroit added two goals for a 4–1 win. Marchand finished with four shots.

goal-63.title: An equalizer before Anaheim pulls away
paragraphs: Marchand tied Anaheim 1–1 at 10:14 of the first period, with Jeff Petry assisting. Florida later took a 3–2 lead, but Anaheim answered with five straight goals to win 7–3. This puck is Marchand’s first-period goal, career No. 431.

goal-64.title: Two goals in a Florida win in Los Angeles
paragraphs: Marchand tied the Kings 2–2 late in the first period, then scored again at 12:36 of the third to complete Florida’s 5–2 win. This puck is the second goal, assisted by Niko Mikkola. Marchand scored twice on three shots as the Panthers finished with four unanswered goals.

goal-65.title: Marchand ends a 13-goal game
paragraphs: Marchand scored unassisted into an empty net with 1:46 left to complete Florida’s 8–5 win over Vancouver. He also assisted on Lundell’s second-period goal. The Panthers had trailed 2–0, then lost a three-goal lead before scoring the game’s final three goals.

goal-66.title: A winning goal against Tampa Bay
paragraphs: Marchand put Florida ahead 3–0 at 11:48 of the second period, finishing a play credited to Verhaeghe and Aaron Ekblad. Tampa Bay later scored twice, making Marchand’s tally the winner in a 5–2 Panthers victory. It was his only shot on goal.

goal-67.title: Three points in Game 7
paragraphs: Marchand helped eliminate Toronto with a goal and two assists in Florida’s 6–1 Game 7 win. He assisted on Lundell’s eventual winner and Luostarinen’s third-period goal before scoring into an empty net at 16:57. This puck is that final goal, which completed the scoring as Florida advanced to the Eastern Conference Final.

goal-68.title: Marchand wins it in overtime
paragraphs: Marchand scored his 22nd career overtime goal to beat Minnesota 4–3, finishing a Verhaeghe assist at 3:00 of the extra period. It was his second goal and third point of the night. He had scored on the power play in the first and assisted on Bennett’s third-period equalizer.

goal-69.title: Two goals bring Boston back within one
paragraphs: Columbus led 5–1 when Marchand scored at 13:07 of the second period. He scored again at 18:37 to cut the lead to 5–4. This puck is the first of those two goals. Marchand also assisted on Bergeron’s short-handed opener, finishing with three points in a 7–4 loss.

goal-70.title: Marchand and Chara trade scoring roles
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Chara’s second-period goal, then scored at 16:21 with Chara and Adam McQuaid earning the assists. His goal put Boston ahead 4–1 in Arizona. The Bruins won 6–2, giving Marchand a goal and an assist in 17:35 of ice time.

goal-71.title: The Perfection Line ties the Rangers
paragraphs: Pastrnak and Bergeron assisted when Marchand tied the game 2–2 at 3:24 of the third period. Mika Zibanejad scored later in the period to give New York a 3–2 win. Marchand finished with four shots, including the goal that briefly erased Boston’s second-period deficit.

goal-72.title: A third-period equalizer in Philadelphia
paragraphs: Marchand tied Philadelphia 2–2 at 5:44 of the third period, just 1:18 after Krejci had scored Boston’s first goal. Krug and Carlo assisted. The two-goal comeback earned Boston overtime, but Philadelphia won 3–2 in a shootout. Marchand put four shots on net.

goal-73.title: Nine shots and a point on both goals
paragraphs: Marchand scored Boston’s power-play equalizer at 7:49 of the second period in Ottawa, then assisted on Krug’s overtime winner. He finished with nine shots and 23:39 of ice time in the 2–1 win. This puck is the tying goal, assisted by Pastrnak and Krug.

goal-74.title: A Perfection Line power-play winner
paragraphs: Marchand broke a 2–2 tie against Nashville at 11:23 of the third period, with Pastrnak and Bergeron assisting. He also assisted on a goal by each linemate, finishing with three points and six shots. Boston scored the final three goals to win 5–2. The puck is signed by all three members of the Perfection Line: Marchand, Bergeron and Pastrnak.

goal-75.title: Two shots, two goals against Buffalo
paragraphs: Marchand scored Boston’s first two goals in a 3–2 win over Buffalo. This puck is his power-play goal at 14:45 of the second period, which put the Bruins ahead 2–1. Grzelcyk and Heinen assisted. Marchand finished with two goals on two shots.

goal-76.title: A short-handed goal in a wild third period
paragraphs: Marchand scored short-handed from a Bergeron assist at 6:49 of the third period to put Boston ahead 4–2 against Los Angeles. He had also assisted on Heinen’s tying goal earlier in the period. The Kings recovered to force overtime, where Bergeron won it 5–4 for Boston.

goal-77.title: Closing out Montreal
paragraphs: Marchand scored into an empty net at 18:37 of the third period, with Loui Eriksson assisting. The goal completed Boston’s 4–1 road win. Bergeron had broken a 1–1 tie in the second period and Pastrnak extended the lead in the third before Marchand supplied the final goal.

milestone-302.title: Five hundred assists
paragraphs: Marchand reached 500 career assists during Boston’s 5–2 win over Montreal. Both of his assists came on power-play goals, first by McAvoy and then by van Riemsdyk. He finished with three shots in 17 minutes. This game-used puck marks the night he reached the assist milestone.

milestone-303.title: Moving past Middleton in points
paragraphs: Two Marchand goals brought his career total to 899 points, moving him past Rick Middleton for fifth in Bruins history. The second tied Colorado 3–3 in the third period before Boston lost in the shootout. This game-used puck preserves the milestone night; Marchand scored on both of his shots.

milestone-304.title: Nine hundred points in St. Louis
paragraphs: Marchand’s first-period goal brought him to 900 career points. He scored again on the power play in the third, giving Boston a lead for the second time that night. McAvoy’s overtime goal settled the 4–3 win. This is a game-used puck from the milestone game.

milestone-305.title: Two goals on the 900-point night
paragraphs: Marchand reached 900 points at 5:02 of the first period, then added another goal at 7:43 of the third. Both gave Boston the lead in a game St. Louis repeatedly tied. The Bruins won 4–3 in overtime. This second game-used artifact shares the milestone with item 304.

milestone-306.title: Eleven straight 20-goal seasons
paragraphs: Marchand set a Bruins record with his 11th consecutive season of at least 20 goals. His third-period goal made it 7–4 against Montreal, and Boston won 9–4. He also assisted on Coyle’s second-period goal. The game-used puck marks a scoring streak that surpassed Bergeron and Johnny Bucyk’s ten-season runs.

milestone-307.title: Passing Bourque with an overtime winner
paragraphs: Marchand’s 396th goal moved him past Ray Bourque into fifth in Bruins history. It also ended the game: he scored from a Coyle assist at 1:48 of overtime to beat Ottawa 3–2. The Senators had erased a two-goal lead. This game-used puck marks the winning night and the career milestone.

milestone-308.title: Two assists in game 1,000
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on both Boston goals in his 1,000th NHL game. The Bruins trailed Tampa Bay 2–0 before McAvoy and van Riemsdyk scored in the second period, each with Marchand and Pastrnak assisting. Tampa Bay won 3–2 in the shootout. Marchand played 23:30 on the milestone night.

milestone-309.title: Goal 400 opens a road win
paragraphs: Marchand scored his 400th NHL goal just 2:12 into Boston’s game at Carolina. Morgan Geekie and Coyle assisted. The Bruins built a three-goal first-period lead and won 4–1. This game-used puck marks the night of the milestone, rather than the specific goal-scored puck.

milestone-310.title: Second on Boston’s playoff points list
paragraphs: Marchand’s two assists brought him to 130 playoff points, moving him ahead of Bergeron and Krejci into second in Bruins history. Both came on DeBrusk power-play goals in the second period of Boston’s 5–1 win over Toronto. This game-used puck marks the opening game of that playoff series.

milestone-311.title: A Bruins record for playoff winners
paragraphs: Marchand’s 12th playoff game-winning goal moved him past Cam Neely for the Bruins record. He scored at 11:53 of the third period in Toronto, then added an empty-net goal for a 4–2 win. An earlier assist on DeBrusk’s goal gave him three points. This game-used puck marks the record-setting night.

milestone-312.title: Boston’s new playoff goals leader
paragraphs: Marchand scored his 56th playoff goal, passing Cam Neely for the Bruins record. His power-play tally at 8:20 of the second period gave Boston a 2–0 lead in Toronto. He later assisted on Pastrnak’s goal in a 3–1 win. This artifact is a game-used puck from that milestone game.

milestone-313.title: A first point against Utah
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Koepke’s goal at 12:49 of the second period in Boston’s first game against Utah Hockey Club. It was Boston’s only goal in a 2–1 overtime loss. This game-used puck records his first point against Utah; the assist puck is cataloged separately as artifact 57.

milestone-314.title: Goal 402 ties Middleton
paragraphs: Marchand tied Rick Middleton for fourth in Bruins goals with No. 402, an overtime winner against Toronto. Pastrnak assisted at 2:26 of the extra period for a 4–3 Boston win. Marchand had earlier assisted on Pastrnak’s power-play goal. This game-used puck marks the two-point night.

milestone-315.title: Passing Esposito with the winner
paragraphs: Marchand’s overtime goal against Toronto was his 78th Bruins game-winner, moving him past Phil Esposito into third in team history. Boston won 4–3 when he scored at 2:26 from a Pastrnak assist. This game-used artifact highlights the winning-goal milestone from the same night as item 314.

milestone-316.title: A milestone puck from Carolina
paragraphs: Marchand passed Rick Middleton with career goal No. 403, taking fourth place on Boston’s goals list. His first-period power-play goal briefly tied Carolina 1–1 before an 8–2 defeat. This artifact is a game-used milestone puck. The actual goal-scored puck is item 42.

milestone-317.title: Marchand wins it with 20 seconds left in overtime
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 4:40 of overtime, with Elias Lindholm assisting, to beat Calgary 4–3. The Flames had erased Boston’s 3–1 lead in the third period. Marchand finished with eight shots. This game-used puck marks the night of his 79th career regular-season game-winner.

milestone-318.title: Game-winner No. 80
paragraphs: Marchand’s only shot of the game broke a 1–1 tie in Detroit at 11:30 of the third period. Boston won 2–1, giving him his 80th career regular-season winning goal. This game-used puck commemorates that milestone; the puck from the goal itself is artifact 43.

milestone-319.title: Two goals in Bruins game 1,053
paragraphs: Marchand moved past Don Sweeney into fourth in Bruins games played, then scored twice in the opening 6:31 against the Islanders. Boston won 6–3. He scored on both of his shots in his 1,053rd appearance. This game-used puck marks the games-played milestone.

milestone-320.title: Another two-goal game
paragraphs: Marchand scored 57 seconds into the game against the Islanders and again at 6:31, his 64th regular-season multi-goal game. The Islanders later tied it 3–3, but Boston scored three unanswered goals in the third to win 6–3. This game-used puck marks Marchand’s two-goal performance.

milestone-321.title: Seven successful penalty shots
paragraphs: Marchand tied Pavel Bure’s NHL record by scoring on his seventh career penalty shot. The goal came at 10:28 of the second period in Seattle, cutting the Kraken’s lead to 2–1. Boston lost 5–1. This game-used milestone puck is separate from the penalty-shot goal puck, item 46.

milestone-322.title: Matching Bergeron’s 81 game-winners
paragraphs: Marchand’s second goal in Chicago was his 81st Bruins game-winner, tying Bergeron for second in team history. He scored twice in 2:05 early in the second period, and Boston won 4–2. This game-used puck commemorates that milestone rather than either of the two goal-scored pucks.

milestone-323.title: His final Boston home game
paragraphs: Marchand recorded seven shots and played 22:11 in a 2–1 loss to the Islanders on February 27, 2025. It became his final home appearance as a Bruin. This game-used puck belongs to that last TD Garden game in Boston colors, when he finished without a point.

milestone-324.title: Seven shots in his last home appearance
paragraphs: Marchand put seven shots on net in 22:11 during his final home appearance as a Bruin. Boston lost 2–1 to the Islanders. This is Kyle Palmieri’s game-winning goal puck from 4:21 of the second period, assisted by Brock Nelson and Adam Pelech. It preserves Marchand’s last night at TD Garden in a Boston uniform, not a goal or assist credited to him.

milestone-325.title: The final game as a Bruin
paragraphs: Marchand played only 2:18 in Boston’s 3–2 win at Pittsburgh on March 1, 2025. It became his final game for the Bruins before his move to Florida. He recorded no points or shots. This game-used puck marks the last appearance, rather than a scoring play.

milestone-326.title: The Boston chapter ends in Pittsburgh
paragraphs: Marchand’s final Bruins appearance was the 3–2 road win over Pittsburgh on March 1, 2025. His night amounted to 2:18 of ice time, with no points or shots. This game-used puck is one of the collection’s three artifacts from his last game in Boston colors.

milestone-327.title: A puck from his last Bruins game
paragraphs: Boston won 3–2 in Pittsburgh, but Marchand’s final appearance for the team lasted just 2:18 of ice time. He did not record a point. This game-used artifact preserves March 1, 2025, alongside items 325 and 326 as the last game of his Bruins tenure.

milestone-328.title: An overtime assist in his Panthers debut
paragraphs: Marchand earned the primary assist on Bennett’s goal at 4:18 of overtime to beat Utah 2–1 in his Florida debut. He recorded four shots in 16:30. This game-used puck marks his first Panthers appearance, which ended with his first point for the team on the winning play.

milestone-329.title: A winning start in Florida
paragraphs: Marchand’s first Florida point came in overtime, when he assisted on Bennett’s winner against Utah. The 2–1 victory on March 28, 2025, was his Panthers debut. He finished with four shots. This second game-used puck from that night shares the debut milestone with artifact 328.

milestone-330.title: His first goal as a Panther
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 16:21 of the second period against Detroit, his first goal for Florida. Balinskis and Luostarinen assisted on the play that made it 3–1. Florida won 4–1, and Marchand scored on his only shot. This game-used puck marks the first-goal night.

milestone-331.title: A goal in game 1,100
paragraphs: Marchand scored Florida’s only goal in his 1,100th NHL game. It came at 5:36 of the second period in Tampa Bay, assisted by Verhaeghe and Matt Kiersted. The Panthers lost 5–1. Marchand played 21:09 and recorded two shots; this game-used puck marks the appearance milestone.

milestone-332.title: His first Florida playoff point helps win the game
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Nate Schmidt’s goal at 4:41 of the second period in Tampa Bay, his first playoff point as a Panther. The goal gave Florida a 3–1 lead and became the winner in a 6–2 game. This game-used puck marks his first postseason appearance for Florida.

milestone-334.title: Back at TD Garden in Florida colors
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Florida’s opening goal just 1:01 into his return to Boston and added another assist in the third period. Verhaeghe scored with 26 seconds remaining for a 4–3 Panthers win. This game-used puck marks Marchand’s first game back against the Bruins at TD Garden.

milestone-335.title: One thousand NHL points
paragraphs: Marchand reached 1,000 career points with two assists in Florida’s 6–3 win over Washington. He helped set up Seth Jones on the power play, then earned the primary assist on Luostarinen’s empty-net goal at 18:30 of the third period. This Panthers game-used puck marks the four-digit milestone.

history-501.title: The Presidents’ Trophy is secured
paragraphs: Marchand played 19:27 and recorded three shots as Boston beat Columbus 2–1 in overtime to clinch the Presidents’ Trophy. Pastrnak scored the winner 41 seconds into overtime. The Bruins stood at 58–12–5 with 121 points. This game-used puck begins the collection’s final eight-game run through the record-setting regular season.

history-502.title: Win 59 in Pittsburgh
paragraphs: Marchand played 18:41 as Boston beat Pittsburgh 4–3, moving to 59–12–5 and 123 points. This puck is McAvoy’s opening goal at 6:20 of the first period, assisted by Zacha and Bertuzzi. Pastrnak scored Boston’s other three goals. Marchand recorded two shots but no points.

history-503.title: Boston reaches 60 wins
paragraphs: Boston earned its 60th victory with a 4–3 shootout win in St. Louis. Marchand played 20:46 and recorded two shots without a point. Boston lost a 3–0 lead before winning in the shootout, reaching 60–12–5 and 125 points.

history-504.title: Coyle ties it, Boston reaches 61 wins
paragraphs: Marchand played 20:38 in Boston’s 2–1 overtime win over Toronto. This puck is Coyle’s tying goal at 11:32 of the third period, assisted by Carlo. Pastrnak scored the overtime winner. Marchand finished without a point as the Bruins reached 61–12–5 and 127 points, one win short of the existing season record.

history-505.title: Boston ties the wins record
paragraphs: Marchand put five shots on net as Boston beat New Jersey 2–1 for its 62nd win. Zacha scored both Bruins goals in the opening 4:44. Boston reached 129 points and tied the NHL single-season wins record. This game-used puck marks that night; Marchand played 18:51 without recording a point.

history-506.title: Sixty-three wins, a new NHL record
paragraphs: Marchand played 18:46 as Boston beat Philadelphia 5–3 for its record-setting 63rd win. This puck is Coyle’s goal 47 seconds into the game, assisted by Clifton. Pastrnak added a hat trick. Marchand finished without a point as the Bruins moved to 63–12–5 and 131 points.

history-507.title: Three Marchand points on a record night
paragraphs: Marchand opened the scoring on the power play and added two assists as Boston beat Washington 5–2. The win brought the Bruins to 133 points, a new NHL single-season record. Bergeron and Pastrnak both assisted on his goal. This is a game-used puck from the points-record night, not Marchand’s goal puck.

history-508.title: The final totals: 65 wins, 135 points
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on DeBrusk’s first-period goal as Boston finished the regular season with a 5–4 win in Montreal. This puck is Pastrnak’s winning goal at 11:00 of the third, assisted by Dmitry Orlov and Bertuzzi. Boston’s final record was 65–12–5, with NHL single-season records of 65 wins and 135 points.

history-509.title: The game puck from win 60
paragraphs: Marchand logged 20:46 in Boston’s 4–3 shootout victory at St. Louis, recording two shots and no points. The Bruins reached 60 wins and 125 points after the Blues erased a three-goal deficit. This is the game-used puck from April 2; the warm-up puck from the same game is item 503.

repeat-600.title: A first playoff point in Panthers red
paragraphs: Marchand opened his first postseason with Florida by setting up Nate Schmidt’s second-period goal for a 3–1 lead. The Panthers went on to beat Tampa Bay 6–2. Marchand played 17:15, put two shots on goal and finished with an assist as Florida took the series opener on the road.

repeat-601.title: Two wins before the trip home
paragraphs: Marchand blocked two shots and delivered two hits in 17:10 as Florida shut out Tampa Bay 2–0. He did not record a point, but the Panthers left Tampa with both opening games won. The result gave his first playoff run with Florida a 2–0 series lead.

repeat-602.title: Marchand helps open the scoring
paragraphs: Marchand supplied the primary assist on Anton Lundell’s goal at 9:06 of the second period, putting Florida ahead first. The Panthers ultimately beat Tampa Bay 4–2 to move within one win of the second round. Marchand finished plus-two with an assist, two hits and a blocked shot.

repeat-603.title: Two assists to close out Tampa Bay
paragraphs: Marchand helped set up Anton Lundell in the first period and Eetu Luostarinen in the third as Florida eliminated Tampa Bay with a 6–3 road win. His two assists brought his total to four for the five-game series. Florida advanced, and Marchand’s first playoff round as a Panther was complete.

repeat-604.title: Two assists in a comeback that fell short
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on goals by Eetu Luostarinen and Uvis Balinskis early in the third period, helping Florida cut Toronto’s 4–1 lead to 4–3. The Panthers could not finish the comeback and lost the second-round opener 5–4. Marchand’s two assists accounted for half of Florida’s goals.

repeat-605.title: The overtime winner Florida needed
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 15:27 of overtime to beat Toronto 5–4 and cut Florida’s series deficit to 2–1. Dmitry Kulikov and Carter Verhaeghe earned the assists. After 23:17 of ice time, Marchand ended a game the Panthers needed to avoid falling three games behind.

repeat-606.title: Nearly 22 minutes to help tie the series
paragraphs: Marchand logged 21:58, three hits and two blocked shots as Florida shut out Toronto 2–0. He did not add a point after his overtime winner two nights earlier. The Panthers nevertheless drew level at two games apiece, turning the series into a best-of-three heading back to Toronto.

repeat-607.title: One win from the conference final
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Sam Bennett’s third-period power-play goal as Florida beat Toronto 6–1 on the road. It was his seventh assist of the playoffs. The Panthers took a 3–2 series lead, putting Marchand one victory away from another trip to the Eastern Conference Final.

repeat-608.title: Three points in Game 7
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on goals by Anton Lundell and Eetu Luostarinen, then scored Florida’s sixth goal with 3:03 remaining. His three-point night helped the Panthers eliminate Toronto 6–1 in Game 7. He finished plus-three as Florida advanced to face Carolina in the Eastern Conference Final.

repeat-609.title: A road win to start the next round
paragraphs: Marchand played 13:01 in Florida’s 5–2 win at Carolina to open the Eastern Conference Final. He was held without a point after his three-point Game 7 in Toronto. The Panthers still took the early series lead, leaving seven more wins between Marchand and a second Stanley Cup.

repeat-610.title: A second road win in Carolina
paragraphs: Marchand played 14:01 as Florida shut out Carolina 5–0 and took a 2–0 lead in the Eastern Conference Final. He finished without a goal or assist. The Panthers had won both games in Raleigh, bringing Marchand two victories from another Stanley Cup Final appearance.

repeat-611.title: A second road win in Carolina
paragraphs: Marchand played 14:01 as Florida shut out Carolina 5–0 and took a 2–0 lead in the Eastern Conference Final. He finished without a goal or assist. The Panthers had won both games in Raleigh, bringing Marchand two victories from another Stanley Cup Final appearance.

repeat-612.title: The sweep slips away
paragraphs: Marchand played 17:27, but neither he nor another Panther could beat Carolina in a 3–0 home loss. Florida’s first chance to finish the Eastern Conference Final ended without a goal. The Panthers still led the series 3–1 and would get another chance to advance in Raleigh.

repeat-613.title: An assist on the way to another Final
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Anton Lundell’s goal at 11:59 of the second period, giving Florida a 3–2 lead. The Panthers won 5–3 in Carolina to finish the series in five games. Marchand was headed back to the Stanley Cup Final, this time with Florida facing Edmonton.

repeat-614.title: An assist on the way to another Final
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Anton Lundell’s goal at 11:59 of the second period, giving Florida a 3–2 lead. The Panthers won 5–3 in Carolina to finish the series in five games. Marchand was headed back to the Stanley Cup Final, this time with Florida facing Edmonton.

repeat-615.title: Short-handed first, then the double-overtime winner
paragraphs: Marchand put Florida ahead with a short-handed goal in the second period, then scored again at 8:05 of double overtime to seal a 5–4 win in Edmonton. Both goals came with assists from Anton Lundell. Marchand’s seven shots and two goals helped tie the Stanley Cup Final at one game each.

repeat-616.title: On the board in 56 seconds
paragraphs: Marchand needed just 56 seconds to open the scoring in Game 3, finishing a play assisted by Anton Lundell and Eetu Luostarinen. Florida went on to beat Edmonton 6–1. Coming straight after his double-overtime winner, the early goal helped give the Panthers a 2–1 lead in the Final.

repeat-617.title: Two goals, one win from the Cup
paragraphs: Marchand opened the scoring at 9:12 of the first period and struck again at 5:12 of the third to put Florida ahead 3–0. The Panthers beat Edmonton 5–2, with his second goal standing as the winner. His two-goal night put Florida one victory from the championship.

repeat-618.title: A second Stanley Cup for Marchand
paragraphs: Marchand lifted the Stanley Cup again after Florida beat Edmonton 5–1 to finish the Final in six games. He did not record a point in the clincher, contributing three hits, two shots and a blocked shot in 15:12. His playoff total stood at 10 goals and 10 assists across 23 games.

repeat-619.title: A second Stanley Cup for Marchand
paragraphs: Marchand lifted the Stanley Cup again after Florida beat Edmonton 5–1 to finish the Final in six games. He did not record a point in the clincher, contributing three hits, two shots and a blocked shot in 15:12. His playoff total stood at 10 goals and 10 assists across 23 games.

repeat-620.title: A second Stanley Cup for Marchand
paragraphs: Marchand lifted the Stanley Cup again after Florida beat Edmonton 5–1 to finish the Final in six games. He did not record a point in the clincher, contributing three hits, two shots and a blocked shot in 15:12. His playoff total stood at 10 goals and 10 assists across 23 games.

repeat-621.title: Two assists to close out Tampa Bay
paragraphs: Marchand helped set up Anton Lundell in the first period and Eetu Luostarinen in the third as Florida eliminated Tampa Bay with a 6–3 road win. His two assists brought his total to four for the five-game series. Florida advanced, and Marchand’s first playoff round as a Panther was complete. This game-used puck represents the game, not a specific goal.

repeat-622.title: One win from the conference final
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Sam Bennett’s third-period power-play goal as Florida beat Toronto 6–1 on the road. It was his seventh assist of the playoffs. The Panthers took a 3–2 series lead, putting Marchand one victory away from another trip to the Eastern Conference Final. This game-used puck represents the game, not a specific goal.

repeat-623.title: Three points in Game 7
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on goals by Anton Lundell and Eetu Luostarinen, then scored Florida’s sixth goal with 3:03 remaining. His three-point night helped the Panthers eliminate Toronto 6–1 in Game 7. He finished plus-three as Florida advanced to face Carolina in the Eastern Conference Final. This game-used puck represents the game, not a specific goal.

repeat-624.title: A second road win in Carolina
paragraphs: Marchand played 14:01 as Florida shut out Carolina 5–0 and took a 2–0 lead in the Eastern Conference Final. He finished without a goal or assist. The Panthers had won both games in Raleigh, bringing Marchand two victories from another Stanley Cup Final appearance. This game-used puck represents the game, not a specific goal.

repeat-625.title: Playoff Point No. 152
paragraphs: Brad Marchand’s 152nd career playoff point gave Florida its first lead in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Final. He earned the lone assist on Anton Lundell’s even-strength goal at 11:59 of the second period, making it 3–2. Florida won 5–3 to clinch the series. Marchand had brought 138 playoff points from Boston; this was his 14th with the Panthers and his 92nd career playoff assist. This puck is from Lundell’s goal.

repeat-626.title: The championship goes into the rafters
paragraphs: Marchand returned for opening night as Florida raised its 2025 championship banner before facing Chicago. He played 20:10 and put four shots on goal in a 3–2 Panthers win. This game belongs to the following regular season, but its ceremony provides the closing scene for the Road to Repeat collection.

milestone-336.title: The assist that made it 1,000
paragraphs: Marchand reached 1,000 career NHL points with his second assist of the night, on Eetu Luostarinen’s empty-net goal with 1:30 remaining. Florida beat Washington 6–3.

milestone-337.title: A celebration, then another goal
paragraphs: Florida honored Marchand’s 1,000th career point before this game against Montreal. He then scored on the power play at 10:18 of the third period, although the Canadiens won 3–2 in overtime.

milestone-338.title: An overtime assist in his Panthers debut
paragraphs: Marchand’s first game with Florida ended with an assist on Sam Bennett’s overtime winner at 4:18. The Panthers beat Utah Hockey Club 2–1 at home. Marchand recorded four shots, two hits and two blocked shots in 16:30.

milestone-339.title: A goal in game 1,100
paragraphs: Marchand scored Florida’s only goal in his 1,100th NHL game. It came at 5:36 of the second period in Tampa Bay, assisted by Verhaeghe and Matt Kiersted. The Panthers lost 5–1. Marchand played 21:09 and recorded two shots; this game-used puck marks the appearance milestone.

hfc-700.title: Marchand starts the comeback
paragraphs: Down 2–0 to Florida, Boston got its first goal from Marchand at 3:38 of the second period. Charlie McAvoy tied it in the third, and Pavel Zacha finished the comeback in overtime, 3–2. Boston held its Hockey Fights Cancer night during its Centennial season.

hfc-701.title: Marchand cuts Florida’s lead
paragraphs: Marchand cut Florida’s two-goal lead in half at 3:38 of the second period, finishing a play credited to Jake DeBrusk and Charlie Coyle. Boston went on to win 3–2 in overtime.

hfc-702.title: A goal, an assist and a comeback
paragraphs: Marchand scored on the power play late in the second period, then assisted on Charlie McAvoy’s third-period goal as Boston recovered from a 4–2 deficit. Matt Grzelcyk tied the game before the Bruins beat New Jersey 5–4 in a shootout. Boston held its Hockey Fights Cancer night at this game; the warm-up puck uses the regular black-and-gold design.

hfc-703.title: HFC night before Marchand’s return
paragraphs: Marchand did not play in Boston’s 3–1 win over Dallas. This purple warm-up puck belongs to the Bruins’ October 25 Hockey Fights Cancer game. David Pastrnak, Taylor Hall and Patrice Bergeron supplied Boston’s goals.

hfc-704.title: No way past Rinne
paragraphs: Marchand and the Bruins were held scoreless in Nashville, where Roman Josi’s first-period goal decided a 1–0 game. The dated purple warm-up puck carries Hockey Fights Cancer branding. The signature on its reverse is preserved without attributing it to a player whose identity has not been verified.

hfc-705.title: A date that never became a game
paragraphs: This Hockey Fights Cancer warm-up puck is printed for Bruins–Hurricanes on December 21, 2021. That game was postponed.

hfc-706.title: A penalty shot brings Boston level
paragraphs: Marchand scored Boston’s only goal on a penalty shot at 4:59 of the second period, tying Toronto 1–1. Auston Matthews answered on the power play, and the Maple Leafs won 2–1. The purple dated warm-up puck marks Toronto’s Hockey Fights Cancer night.

warmup-707.title: Two assists on his return to Boston
paragraphs: Marchand returned to TD Garden as a Panther and set up goals by Mackie Samoskevich and Eetu Luostarinen. Florida won 4–3 on Carter Verhaeghe’s goal with 26 seconds remaining.

hfc-708.title: Marchand helps bring Boston level
paragraphs: Marchand earned the secondary assist when Patrice Bergeron tied the game 1–1 at 1:05 of the third period. Pittsburgh answered with goals from Brandon Sutter and Jussi Jokinen and held on for a 3–2 win. Marchand finished with one assist in 15:40 of ice time. This purple Penguins game-used puck comes from Pittsburgh’s October 30, 2013 Hockey Fights Cancer night.

warmup-710.title: Marchand helps turn the third period
paragraphs: Boston trailed Montreal 2–1 entering the third. Marchand supplied the lone assist on Charlie McAvoy’s power-play equalizer at 2:14, starting a four-goal Bruins period and a 5–2 win.

warmup-711.title: A goal and an assist in an eleven-goal game
paragraphs: Marchand scored at 8:49 of the second period and later set up Patrice Bergeron on the power play. Boston still needed two late goals to win 6–5 in Seattle: Brandon Carlo tied it with 3:41 left, and Jake DeBrusk scored the winner with 1:38 remaining.

warmup-712.title: Three points to erase a two-goal deficit
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on David Pastrnak’s first-period goal, tied the game on the power play at 18:58, then put Boston ahead 33 seconds into the second. The Bruins beat Vegas 4–3. This rainbow-logo warm-up puck is printed for Pride Night.

warmup-714.title: A power-play assist in Buffalo
paragraphs: Marchand assisted on Hampus Lindholm’s power-play goal at 12:23 of the second period, extending Boston’s lead to 5–0. The Bruins beat Buffalo 5–2.

warmup-715.title: Boston’s first visit to Utah
paragraphs: Marchand set up Cole Koepke for Boston’s only goal at 12:49 of the second period. Utah tied it late in regulation and won 2–1 in overtime. The warm-up puck carries Utah’s inaugural-season logo and marks the Bruins’ first game against the Utah Hockey Club.

warmup-716.title: Through to the conference final
paragraphs: Marchand was held without a point as Boston shut out Columbus 3–0 in Game 6 to win the second-round series 4–2. David Krejci, Marcus Johansson and David Backes scored. Boston went on to reach the Stanley Cup Final.

hfc-717.title: An HFC night on the Chicago trip
paragraphs: A night after his three-point game in Minnesota, Marchand played in Florida’s 5–1 win at Chicago without recording a point. The Panthers scored four times in the third period. Chicago designated this game Hockey Fights Cancer night, although the warm-up puck uses its black-and-red Centennial design.

milestone-340.title: Captain for the Centennial Game
paragraphs: Marchand captained Boston in its Centennial Game against Montreal, exactly 100 years after the Bruins’ first NHL game. Boston won 6–3, with two goals each from Charlie McAvoy and Charlie Coyle. Marchand did not record a point; this game-used puck commemorates the anniversary itself.

milestone-341.title: Marchand wins it in overtime
paragraphs: Marchand scored twice and added an assist in Florida’s 4–3 overtime win at Minnesota. He scored on the power play in the first, assisted on Sam Bennett’s third-period equalizer, then ended the game at 3:00 of overtime. This game-used puck commemorates the three-point performance; it is not identified as either goal-scored puck.

history-510.title: Win 61 on the Road to History
paragraphs: Marchand played in Boston’s 2–1 overtime win over Toronto, though he did not record a point. Charlie Coyle tied it in the third, and David Pastrnak scored in overtime. The Bruins reached 61–12–5 and 127 points after game 78.

warmup-713.title: A goal on his 1,000-point celebration night
paragraphs: Florida celebrated Marchand’s 1,000th NHL point before facing Montreal. He added another that night, opening the scoring on the power play at 10:18 of the third period. Sam Bennett and Seth Jones supplied the assists. Marchand finished with four shots in 19:09, but Montreal erased Florida’s two-goal lead and won 3–2 in overtime.
